linguistic_propositions.proposition: The prefix-conjugated verb has exactly three mood states.
For the nun-bearing class the second and third moods are surface-identical and only the licensor distinguishes them.
Weak-final imperfects retain the weak letter in the second mood but delete it in the third.
A conditional particle places both the condition verb and the answer verb in the third mood.
A conditional noun can itself act as the licensor of the third mood.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: Word-initial hamza divides into a type that is always pronounced and a type pronounced only utterance-initially.
The definite article, commands of triliteral verbs, perfects of the five- and six-letter derived patterns, and a short closed noun list take the connecting type.
Most nouns, all particles, three- and four-letter perfects and the first-person imperfect take the cutting type.
The closed noun list has seven members.
In connected speech the connecting hamza vanishes and the preceding vowel links to the following consonant.
In pointed text the two types are distinguished by the presence of the hamza mark.
In unpointed text the distinction is not recoverable from the orthography and must come from lexical or morphological knowledge.
The vowel of a connecting alif on a command follows the stem vowel of the imperfect, defaulting to kasra.
The elative pattern built on a hamza-initial root merges the two hamzas into a long alif.
Elatives take the cutting type because they are nominal.

linguistic_propositions.proposition: A hollow verb is one whose middle radical is a weak letter.
The long medial vowel is retained before vowel-initial suffixes and shortened before consonant-initial ones.
Verbs with one weak middle radical shorten to a damma and those with the other shorten to a kasra.
A subset shortens to a kasra despite the radical, because the underlying pattern carried a kasra.
In the imperfect the long vowel is kept throughout the paradigm.
In the third mood both the final ending and the medial vowel shorten.
The surface long vowel of a hollow verb is not a radical and the certified root supplies the weak letter it stands for.
Hollow and weak-final are distinct classes distinguished by which radical position is weak.
The shortened vowel's quality can be predicted from the middle radical alone.

misleading_shortcuts: 'the imperfect keeps the long vowel throughout' is contradicted within the same paradigm by the consonant-suffixed persons
'first weak radical gives a damma, second gives a kasra' is a surface heuristic that the lesson's own exception subset defeats
'the third mood shortens both vowels' omits the condition that no vowel-initial suffix follows
the memorisation table can be learned as a list of surfaces without the conditioning rule that produces them
the long alif can be read as a radical alif unless the root is certified independently
nahw_relevance: medium - the third mood is the syntactic trigger for the double shortening, so mood assignment and morphological realisation have to be resolved together
new_knowledge: the hollow class as a named class with its own conditioning environment
suffix-type conditioning as the trigger for a medial alternation
quality selection from the underlying pattern vowel, not from the surface
the interaction of mood with a medial phonological alternation
an explicit contrast against the weak-final class
paradigms: a full perfect paradigm across all persons showing where the vowel is long and where it is short
a full imperfect paradigm across all persons with the same alternation
a mood table stepping one hollow verb through the three moods
a reference table of common hollow verbs giving root, imperfect and third-mood form
prerequisite_knowledge: the three moods and their exponents
root-and-pattern analysis with three radical positions
recognition of weak letters as radicals
perfect and imperfect person suffixes
procedures: certify the root and locate the weak position
classify the verb as hollow rather than weak-final from that position
identify whether the suffix about to be attached begins with a vowel or a consonant
retain or shorten the medial vowel accordingly
select the shortened vowel's quality from the underlying radical together with the pattern vowel
in the third mood, apply the medial shortening as well as the ending change
recognition_criteria: a long medial vowel in the citation form where a root position is expected
alternation of that long vowel with a short one across the paradigm of one lexeme
a consonant-initial suffix directly following the medial position
a certified root whose middle position holds a weak letter
a third-mood form shorter than its imperfect by both a medial and a final element
required_evidence: a certified root with the weak position located, the pattern vowel for quality selection, the suffix type in the environment, and the mood where the third mood is involved
reuses_from_earlier: L2.M1.04 and L2.M1.05 third-mood exponents, now interacting with medial shortening
L2.M1.06 command derivation, applied here to a hollow verb
root-and-pattern analysis from earlier morphology work
rich_hover_relevance: a hover on a hollow surface must show the certified root with the weak position marked and state that the visible long vowel realises that radical, otherwise the letter count and the radical count disagree with no explanation
sarf_relevance: high - the class assignment, the conditioning environment and the vowel-quality selection are all root-and-pattern decisions, and the surface long vowel actively conceals the radical
tutor_drill_relevance: supports environment-recognition drills on suffix type, quality-selection drills including the exception subset, and mood-plus-morphology drills where both changes must be applied at once
uncertainty_flags: the imperfect is said to keep the long vowel throughout and is then contradicted by its own paradigm
the quality rule is presented as radical-based with the pattern-based exception relegated to a footnote, although the exception is what actually governs the rule
the third-mood double shortening is stated without the no-vowel-suffix condition
the hamza-final member of the class is included in the lists without addressing its extra complications

proposed_new_units.summary: Selector predicting, for a hollow lexeme in a given environment, whether the medial vowel is retained or shortened and which short vowel results, taking the certified weak radical together with the underlying pattern vowel as inputs and abstaining where the pattern vowel is unrecorded.
proposed_new_units.why_existing_insufficient: u-s06 assigns the weak class and warns against reading the long alif as a radical, and u-s07 owns transformation chains in general, but neither records the pattern vowel that decides the shortened quality, which is the one input the surface cannot supply.

worked_analysis_stages: give the citation form
give the root with the weak position marked
identify the suffix type
give the resulting surface with its retained or shortened vowel
